claims.text: Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi tends to exhibit compositional segregation.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi tends to exhibit residual thermal stresses.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi tends to exhibit defect formation.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will produce denser AlCrFeNiSi than conventional bulk fabrication.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will produce more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi with less elemental segregation.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will lower residual stress in AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional fabrication.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
Binder jetting can form a binder-containing green body at ambient temperature before isothermal sintering.
Approximately 1000–1400 °C is a typical sintering range for consolidation of the proposed AlCrFeNiSi HEA.
Controlled, slow cooling preserves the interdiffusion benefits of sintered AlCrFeNiSi.
The isothermal sintering phase enables full interdiffusion of the constituent elements.
Full interdiffusion during isothermal sintering promotes structural homogeneity and minimizes compositional gradients.
Binder jetting minimizes thermal gradients during part formation because it creates a near-net-shape green body without beam melting.
Interdiffusion and isothermal sintering reduce localized stresses.
Interdiffusion and isothermal sintering reduce defects that would otherwise arise during rapid cooling.
Binder-jet/sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have lower porosity than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Binder-jet/sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have higher compressive strength than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Binder-jet/sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have higher toughness than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Casting or laser-based additive manufacturing produces measurable segregation, residual stress buildup, and defects in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed benefits require sufficient interdiffusion within the 1000–1400 °C range and controlled cooling.

contradictions.description: The baseline combines casting and laser-based additive manufacturing as a single conventional comparator, while the experiment requires the comparator to use identical sintering-temperature conditions. Casting and laser-based routes do not ordinarily have a directly corresponding sintering-temperature condition, so the stated control is internally ambiguous.
